Historical analysis shows: Every peaceful movement that gets **{{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}} active support** succeeds.

- $8 \text{ billion humans} \times 3.5\% = 280 \text{ million}$
- The strategy requires 280 million individuals to vote YES on a [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty-academic.qmd)
- That is achievable. The methodology follows.

## The Message That Spreads

### What Does Not Go Viral

- "Please donate to clinical trials" (boring)
- "Policy proposal for healthcare reform" (sleep-inducing)
- "Consider supporting this initiative" (ignored)

### What Does Go Viral

- "Humanity has [13,000 nukes](../references.qmd#world-warheads) but no cure for a child's cancer" (rage-inducing)
- "Taxpayers spend $340/year on killing people, $8/year on curing them" (shocking)
- "{{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} investment returns while saving humanity" (greed + altruism)

## The Viral Formula

$$
\text{Emotion} + \text{Personal Stake} + \text{Shareability} = \text{Viral}
$$

### Emotional Triggers

- **Anger**: "[FDA delays kill more than the drugs](../references.qmd#fda-drug-lag-deaths-estimate)"
- **Fear**: "Humans will die of disease, not war"
- **Hope**: "Society could cure this in 10 years"
- **Greed**: "{{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} annual returns forever"

### Personal Stake

- "Tax revenue allocation: $340 to war, $8 to cures"
- "Family members die while bureaucrats meet"
- "Pediatric rare diseases: $0 funding"

### Shareability

- One-sentence summary
- Shocking statistic
- Clear call to action

## The Content Ladder

### Level 1: The Hook (3 seconds)

**"Humanity spends {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}}X more on weapons than testing which medicines work"**

- Simple
- Shocking
- Shareable

### Level 2: The Emotion (30 seconds)

**"While someone reads this, 50 people died of preventable disease. Society has the money to cure them. Humans spend it on weapons instead."**

### Level 3: The Solution (3 minutes)

**"A 1% treaty: Redirect 1% of military spending to pragmatic clinical trials. Fund trials that are {{< var trial_cost_reduction_factor >}}× cheaper. Cure major diseases in 10 years. Everyone wins."**

### Level 4: The Action (immediate)

**"Vote YES. Buy bonds. Share this."**

## Platform-Specific Strategies

### Twitter/X

- Death counter bots: "147 died while users scrolled"
- Spending comparisons: Daily updates
- Quote politicians saying they care
- Then show their votes for war budgets

### TikTok/Reels

- 15-second videos: "Guess what taxes buy"
- Before/after: Dystopia 2050 vs Wishonia 2050
- Doctors explaining why they cannot cure patients
- Patients explaining why they are dying

### YouTube

- Long-form explainers
- Interviews with doctors
- Financial breakdown of VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds
- Debate: "Is curing disease profitable?"

### Reddit

- AMAs with researchers
- Data visualizations
- "ELI5: Why does a specific rare disease lack treatment?"
- Financial analysis of bonds

## The Referral System

### Individual Incentives

- Share with 10 people → Entered in bond lottery
- Acquiring 100 votes → Free VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bond
- Reach influencer status → Speaking opportunities

### Influencer Incentives

- 1M views discussing treaty → $10K in bonds
- Convert followers to voters → Bonus VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bond allocation
- Top promoter → Named institute

### Corporate Incentives

- Companies that promote treaty → Tax benefits
- Employee participation programs → Matching bonds
- PR value: "We're saving humanity"

## The Meme Arsenal

### Economic Memes

- "Raytheon CEO salary vs rare disease research funding"
- "[Cost of one F-35](../references.qmd#f35-cost-vs-rare-disease-research) = ~160 Oxford-style trials"
- "Society has money for 13,000 nukes but not essential insulin"

### Emotional Memes

- "Why is a child dying while governments build Skynet?"
- "Imagine if humanity spent weapons money on cures"
- "The government chose missiles over parents"

### Comparison Memes

- "Military budget breaks the screen / Clinical trials barely visible"
- "Days to approve weapons: 1 / Days to approve cancer cure: [6,205](../references.qmd#research-to-practice-gap)"

## The Influencer Strategy

### Target Categories

**Health/Wellness** (100M+ followers combined):

- This group already cares about health
- The audience is health-conscious
- Natural fit for cure advocacy

**Finance/Investment** (50M+ followers):

- "{{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns is compelling content"
- Financial analysis is their specialty
- Greed motivates sharing

**Gaming/Tech** (200M+ followers):

- Young, internet-native
- Understand decentralization
- Dislike bureaucracy

**Political** (150M+ followers):

- Both left and right can support
- Bipartisan message
- Career-making position

### The Pitch to Influencers

"Make one video about a 1% treaty:

- Guaranteed to go viral (emotional + controversial)
- Positions the creator as visionary
- Potential to save millions of lives
- Plus: Offer them bonds"

## The Data That Spreads

### Daily Updates

- "Today's death toll: [150,000](../references.qmd#who-daily-deaths)"
- "Total spent on war today: ~$7.4 billion"
- "Total spent on cures today: [$186 million](../references.qmd#global-gov-med-research-spending)"
- "Ratio: Still insane"

### Personal Calculators

- "Individual tax contribution to war: $340"
- "Individual tax contribution to cures: $8"
- "If one redirected 1%: Lives saved: 0.003"

### Comparison Tools

- "A city's military spending could fund X trials"
- "A state's military budget could cure Y diseases"

## The Controversy Strategy

### High-Engagement Assertions

- "[FDA has killed more Americans than terrorists](../references.qmd#fda-drug-lag-deaths-estimate)"
- "NIH is a [$48B](../references.qmd#nih-budget-fy2025) jobs program, not a cure program"
- "Individual votes do not matter (Princeton proved it)"
- "Governments are building Skynet while patients die"

### Expected Pushback (and Responses)

**"The proposal is oversimplified!"**

→ "And critics are overcomplicating. People are dying."

**"This will never work!"**

→ "[Oxford RECOVERY trial](../references.qmd#recovery-trial-summary-quote) already proved it works."

**"The military needs its budget!"**

→ "The treaty takes 1%. Nations keep 99%. This is stable."

## The Metrics

### Viral Success Indicators

- **Phase 1** (Month 1-3): 10M aware
- **Phase 2** (Month 4-6): 100M engaged
- **Phase 3** (Month 7-12): 280M committed

### Conversion Funnel

- **Aware**: Saw the message
- **Engaged**: Clicked, read, watched
- **Shared**: Told others
- **Committed**: Voted YES or bought bonds

### Target Ratios

- 1 billion aware → 500M engaged → 280M committed
- Share rate: 50% (if content is good)
- Commitment rate: 56% (if message resonates)

## The Timeline (Years 1-2 of the Roadmap)

This viral marketing campaign builds awareness and support during the first 18 months, preparing for the treaty push in months 19-36. See [The Roadmap](roadmap-academic.qmd) for the complete 3-year plan.

### Months 1-6: Foundation & Launch

- Launch website and core content
- Recruit first 100,000 advocates
- Influencer partnerships begin
- Viral campaigns and media coverage

### Months 7-12: Acceleration

- Reach 100M people aware
- Scale referral program
- Political pressure begins building

### Months 13-18: Critical Mass

- 280M voters committed
- Media saturation
- Politicians feel pressure
- Ready for treaty push (months 19-36)
- Mainstream coverage

## The Strategy

The campaign does not ask people to donate.
It does not ask people to change.
It asks them to **vote for not dying**.

That is the easiest thing to make go viral.

Because everyone, eventually, does not want to die.
